title: Pulmonary Embolism Response Team Germany, Austria, Confoederatio Helvetica-Registry
summary:
Acute pulmonary embolism (PE) occurs when a blood clot blocks one or more vessels in the lungs. The clot usually originates from the veins in the legs or pelvis and is carried to the lungs by the bloodstream. As a result, part of the lung is no longer adequately supplied with blood and oxygen. This can lead to sudden shortness of breath, chest pain, rapid heartbeat, dizziness, or even heart failure. PE is a medical emergency and must be treated quickly. After heart attack and stroke, PE is the third most common cause of death from cardiovascular diseases.

Because there are many different and sometimes complicated treatment options for patients with acute PE, special teams called "Pulmonary Embolism Response Teams" (PERT) are being formed in the USA and increasingly in Europe. These PERTs consist of experts from various medical fields and can be quickly assembled when needed. The goal of these teams is to work together quickly to find the best, individually tailored treatment for each patient.

The aim of this registry is to systematically record and evaluate the use of such expert teams (PERTs) in the treatment of patients with acute PE in Germany, Austria, and Switzerland.

interventions.name:
Adult patients diagnosed with pulmonary embolism (PE) who have been managed with the involvement of a pulmonary embolism response team (PERT) in the decision-making process for their treatment.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
- Informed consent
- Age 18 years or older
- Confirmed PE diagnosis
- PERT consultation and decision regarding treatment
Exclusion criteria:
There are no exclusion criteria.
